articles.title: Plans Approved for 23 New Homes in Kirkholt
articles.excerpt: A new development of 23 homes, including an apartment block and terraced houses, has been approved for the Kirkholt estate, aiming to provide affordable housing for local residents.
articles.content_html:
Plans for a new housing development in Kirkholt have been approved, which will see the construction of 23 homes, including a block of apartments and five terraced houses. The development is located off Queen’s Drive and is being led by Mosscare St Vincent Housing (MSV), a not-for-profit Registered Provider.

The new homes will be available for social rent, priced at approximately 60 per cent of market rates, addressing the local demand for affordable housing. The apartment block will consist of one-bedroom units, while the terraced houses will each feature four bedrooms. The site, which has remained vacant since the demolition of an old block of flats in 2009, was previously used temporarily by Kirkholt Medical Practice before relocating to a permanent facility nearby.

Planning documents highlight the importance of this development in revitalising a prominent site within the community. The proposal aims to create a sustainable and high-quality living environment that meets local housing needs and helps mitigate issues related to anti-social behaviour associated with the disused land.

In addition to the housing project, plans for a community garden, to be managed by Q Gardens, were also approved last month. This initiative is expected to enhance the local area and promote community engagement. The development is seen as a significant step towards creating a balanced community and increasing the availability of affordable housing in Kirkholt.

articles.title: Rochdale Council Launches Preparing for Adulthood Strategy for Young People in Care
articles.excerpt: Rochdale Council has introduced a new strategy to support young people in care as they transition to adulthood, aiming to provide clearer pathways and necessary resources.
articles.content_html:
Rochdale Council has launched its new Preparing for Adulthood strategy, aimed at supporting young people in care as they transition into adulthood. The initiative was unveiled at a special event held at Spotland Mills, where young people, councillors, members of Rochdale’s Parents Carers Voice, and council staff gathered to discuss the importance of this support.

The strategy focuses on young people aged 14 to 25 and seeks to make their journey into adulthood easier and more positive. The council's Preparing for Adulthood Team will assist young individuals in finding appropriate support as they move from children's services to adult social care. Before reaching the age of 18, the council will conduct an assessment to identify each young person's care and support needs.

For those deemed eligible, a new support plan will be developed to help them continue their education, acquire new skills, and access any additional support required by them or their families. The event featured contributions from young people who highlighted the significance of feeling valued and supported during this critical transition period.

The launch of this strategy is a crucial step in ensuring that young people in care receive the guidance and resources they need to thrive as they enter adulthood. The council's commitment to this initiative reflects its dedication to improving the lives of vulnerable young individuals in the community.
